manifest.name: Rullst
manifest.workers: Tokio multi-threaded runtime, one worker per available CPU (2)
manifest.database_layer: rullst-orm (#[derive(Orm)] with RowSnapshot: find, save, all, query builder; SQLx PostgreSQL pool)

phase2.validation: ValidatedJson and ValidatedForm (#[derive(Validate)]: constraint failures 422, unreadable bodies 400); GET /worlds: Query (400) and FieldErrors::validate (422); Path<i32> (400)

csrf.mechanism: csrf_middleware on /form and /login only: double-submit rullst_csrf cookie, token masked per response in the _token field, compared in constant time; 403

session.mechanism: session registry as cargo rullst auth generates it: rullst_session cookie sealed with APP_KEY, one rullst_auth_sessions row per sign-in, read by primary key on every request

manifest.notes: Rullst router, ORM and html! without the Server middleware stack; comparable to the Axum app.
manifest.listing_note: Serves its router through rullst::web::axum::serve, Axum's own server re-exported by Rullst, and bypasses rullst::Server, so none of the production middleware that cargo rullst new generates runs; its Hello world numbers are therefore largely Axum's. No other framework has such a stripped-down variant here, so it is listed apart from the headline tables.
manifest.role_note: Rullst's router, ORM and html! served without the production middleware that cargo rullst new generates, comparable to the Axum app. It is not how Rullst sets up an application, so it is a diagnostic shown next to the reference, with scores and without a position; Rullst as generated is the ranked Rullst.
